svg.title: The read-only diagnostic pipeline, from a question to a checkable verdict
svg.desc: A pipeline in four stages, left to right. The first stage, on the client side of a dashed protocol boundary, is a person asking the host why checkout is failing, and the host's model choosing a tool, carried by a single tools/call request with no session and no handshake. The remaining three stages are on the server side. The second lists five read tools, list_pods, describe_pod, get_events, get_logs and list_deployments, and notes that each makes one blocking Kubernetes call routed through a single helper onto a worker thread, because on the event loop the whole transport stalls. The third stage holds four cards for the same failure read from four API fields: the pod phase, which says Running and looks fine; the container's waiting state, which says CrashLoopBackOff and gives no cause; the container's previous terminated state, outlined in green because its exit code is the cause; and the events, a BackOff seen forty-two times. A note says that reading one and stopping gets a confident wrong answer. The fourth stage is the verdict: crash_loop at high confidence, a findings list where each entry names the API field it came from so a human can check it with kubectl, a next steps list carrying the exact next call with its arguments filled in, and the pure analyse function that produced them, which touches no network and is tested with no cluster. A band across the bottom, starting at the protocol boundary, states that read-only here is structural rather than advisory: neither read module contains a delete, patch, create or replace call, and readOnlyHint prevents nothing, while the test that greps both modules does.
svg.text: The diagnostic pipeline: a question, then a checkable verdict
Four stages, one direction. Every stage reads, and no stage has a path to a write.
Read one and stop and you get
it came from, so a human
so it is tested with no cluster.
Neither read module contains a delete_, patch_, create_, or replace_ call.
readOnlyHint is only a hint: it prevents nothing. The test that greps both modules is what prevents it.
